name: UK energy price cap
summary: Ofgem sets the January cap by 25 Nov; forecasts put it 26–28% above the current £1,723
state: The cap for a typical dual-fuel household is £1,723 a year from 1 Oct. As of 21 Nov Ofgem had not announced the January to March 2027 cap, which is due on or before 25 Nov. Cornwall Insight forecast a 26% rise to about £2,166 on 18 Nov (IBTimes), and an average of supplier predictions compiled by Uswitch points to about 28% (Uswitch, 19 Nov). Both are above the 20% Alert line.
for_you: Households on standard variable tariffs and prepayment meters are most exposed to a January rise. Ofgem's announcement on or before 25 Nov will confirm the level; help for those struggling is listed on Ofgem's website.
rubric_hit: Alert: forecast rise ≥ 20% (Cornwall Insight 26%, supplier average 28% for January)

sources.title: IBTimes UK — Energy bills could rise 26% in January, Cornwall Insight warns

why: The Ofgem cap sets bills for most UK households — a direct cost-of-living signal.
drivers: Wholesale gas and power prices, network costs, policy levies.

rubric.normal: Typical dual-fuel cap < £1,700/yr and next forecast change < +5%.
